text: Gives the rollout as ordered, numbered steps, from putting the keys in the store through to revoking the old keys, with no point where customer requests fail.
States the startup behaviour: all three keys are loaded before the app reports ready, the load retries 3 times 2 seconds apart, and the process exits non-zero if the store is still unreachable.

States the runtime refresh: secrets are re-read every 5 minutes, the last good value is kept with a warning when a read fails, and values exist only in process memory, never on disk, in environment variables or in logs.
States the access rules: orders-api-prod has read-only access to orders-api/prod/* only, only the security on-call writes prod secrets, and engineers cannot read prod values.
Rotates all three keys at their providers because git history is not rewritten, and revokes each old key only after every running instance is confirmed to be using the new one.
Adds a CI check that fails any change putting an api_key back into config/app.yaml.
Explains how local development gets keys without reading prod secrets.
Marks scheduled rotation (whether, and how often) as an open, undecided question rather than choosing a cadence.
